parameters.name: y0
parameters.description: State translation `y0 = 1` U_y, chosen before polynomial fitting as a convenient origin close to the observed lower state range; it is not a known physical zero.

parameters.name: s0
parameters.description: State scale `s0 = 1` U_y, chosen to make `(y-y0)/s0` dimensionless without changing its numerical value.

parameters.name: u0
parameters.description: Input scale `u0 = 60` U_x1, chosen as a convenient near-central scale from inspection of training input magnitudes, not fitted.

parameters.name: v0
parameters.description: Input scale `v0 = 20` U_x2, chosen as a convenient near-central scale from inspection of training input magnitudes, not fitted.

parameters.name: c0
parameters.description: Coefficient multiplying `1`, jointly estimated by final rollout least squares; initial value came from the training-only fits described in estimation.

parameters.name: c1
parameters.description: Coefficient multiplying `((y-y0)/s0)`, jointly estimated by final rollout least squares; initial value came from the training-only fits described in estimation.

parameters.name: c2
parameters.description: Coefficient multiplying `(x1/u0)`, jointly estimated by final rollout least squares; initial value came from the training-only fits described in estimation.

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: Nonnegative state-normalization coefficient in `1+k*((y-y0)/s0)**2`, jointly estimated with numerator coefficients.

estimation.criterion: Sum of squared full-rollout state residuals `y_sim-y` over every row after the first in each file. Each rollout uses classical fourth-order Runge–Kutta, one step of `5` s, with `x1` and `x2` held at the left sample. This matches the supplied evaluation objective rather than treating the sampled derivative as an instantaneous derivative.
estimation.data: All rows of `data/train.csv` and `data/val.csv`, treated as two separately initialized uninterrupted trajectories, with sampling period `5` s from TASK.md. No measured-state resets inside either file and no rows removed. Validation was first used for structure comparison, then explicitly included in final calibration to use both available excitation patterns. Final validation errors are calibration diagnostics, not independent generalization estimates.
estimation.method: Final parameters were estimated jointly with nonlinear least squares using `scipy.optimize.least_squares`, trust-region reflective method, `jac` supplied by forward sensitivity propagation through all four RK4 stages, and `x_scale = "jac"`. This uses the exact chosen rollout and avoids finite-difference Jacobian cost; ordinary least squares cannot minimize its nonlinear trajectory objective. Parameter optimization coordinates are scaled by `Max(Abs(initial_value),0.01)`, a dimensionless numerical conditioning rule implemented in `refine.py`. The stopping tolerances `ftol = 1e-8`, `xtol = 1e-8`, and `gtol = 1e-8` are dimensionless solver settings; the maximum is `120` function evaluations. Final optimization is deterministic and uses no random seed. The bound `k >= 0` is an assumed regularity constraint, not a measured property. The first `10` numerator coefficients were initialized by the degree-two training derivative ordinary least-squares solution, and `k = 0` was the initial rational denominator. Training-only rollout refinement supplied the numeric final-stage start listed below. Actual final-stage starts: `c0 = -0.0034863817744944571` U_y/s; `c1 = -0.3121391641211782` U_y/s; `c2 = -0.012591251624965783` U_y/s; `c3 = 0.025229344676053724` U_y/s; `c4 = -0.0026374772881981195` U_y/s; `c5 = 0.18831458036944868` U_y/s; `c6 = 0.028508906059026336` U_y/s; `c7 = 0.011914435701962432` U_y/s; `c8 = -0.0085716851390651109` U_y/s; `c9 = 0.0034359334072820913` U_y/s; `k = 1.0511472105027841`. These starts were used because the training-only rollout fits had already produced finite plausible trajectories. No random numbers apply.

discussion.family: Rational nonlinear state-space vector field: quadratic polynomial numerator and positive quadratic state denominator. Rational model-family context: N. M. Mangan, S. L. Brunton, J. L. Proctor and J. N. Kutz, Inferring Biological Networks by Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics, IEEE Transactions on Molecular, Biological and Multi-Scale Communications 2, 52–63, 2016, DOI 10.1109/TMBMC.2016.2633265 (publisher bibliographic record checked). This fit is not sparse implicit SINDy.
discussion.interpretation: The actual units are not supplied. `U_y`, `U_x1`, and `U_x2` denote placeholders for the unknown units of `y`, `x1`, and `x2`; `s` denotes seconds. Normalized features and exponents are dimensionless. The numerator terms `c0*1 + c1*((y-y0)/s0) + c2*(x1/u0) + c3*(x2/v0) + c4*((y-y0)/s0)**2 + c5*((y-y0)/s0)*(x1/u0) + c6*((y-y0)/s0)*(x2/v0) + c7*(x1/u0)**2 + c8*(x1/u0)*(x2/v0) + c9*(x2/v0)**2` give constant drift, state feedback, input forcing and their quadratic interactions. Division by `1+k*((y-y0)/s0)**2` progressively attenuates the whole vector field away from the chosen state origin. `k >= 0` makes the denominator at least `1`, so there are no denominator poles. All terms have mathematical rather than established physical interpretations.
discussion.origin: The quadratic derivative fit was substantially better than the affine baseline, but full-trajectory errors remained state dependent. A positive state-dependent denominator was therefore a guessed smooth rate attenuation, tested after polynomial and input-dependent damping models. The numerator keeps the full degree-two polynomial library; no term was selected by a physical assumption. The denominator was chosen instead of higher numerator degree as a compact alternative. The nonnegative denominator constraint was retained for domain safety.
discussion.limitations: No physical apparatus, units, measurement noise model or intended operating envelope is known. Inputs and the state are correlated along only two supplied files, so the fitted coefficients need not be separately causally identifiable. One anomalous middle transition occurs in each file; it was not used as a reset. Oscillatory serially correlated derivative residuals remain, consistent with omitted dynamics or timing effects but not proof of their cause; an autonomous scalar state with only the two current inputs cannot explicitly represent input history. Extrapolation beyond the supplied excitation is unvalidated. Although its denominator is globally positive, bounded-input global trajectory stability is not established.
